segments.title: Chương 88: 0088【Tôi chọn 404】
segments.content:
Chen Guiliang strode ahead. "What's your name?"

The male student said, "My name is Jiang Junlai, from Guizhou."

"How did you end up choosing the Yuanpei Program?" Chen Guiliang acted like a senior interrogating a junior.

Jiang Junlai had no doubt about his identity and explained in great detail, "After the CMO, I received guaranteed admission. I originally wanted to apply for the math department. You know, senior, Beida's math department is especially awesome. That night, a Teacher Zhu came, I've already forgotten what he said to me, but somehow I ended up applying for the Yuanpei Program in a daze."

"You didn't make the wrong choice," Chen Guiliang said, holding back a laugh.

Jiang Junlai asked curiously, "Which school are you from, senior?"

Chen Guiliang said, "I'm also in the Yuanpei Program."

Jiang Junlai was overjoyed. "That's great! What year are you, senior?"

"First year," Chen Guiliang replied.

"Huh?" Jiang Junlai suspected he had misheard.

Chen Guiliang turned his head. "Let's go, what are you still standing there for?"

Jiang Junlai's tone was a little annoyed. "Do you know how to get to the dorms?"

"No." Chen Guiliang continued to stroll forward.

Looking at the guy in front of him, Jiang Junlai felt a herd of ten thousand alpacas stampeding through his heart. At this moment, all he wanted to do was roar: Good heavens, what kind of lunatic is this!

But he really couldn't find the dorm, and subconsciously chased after him for a few steps. "You're just walking randomly without asking first?"

"Where did you ask before?" Chen Guiliang retorted.

Jiang Junlai said, "I first asked the gate guard, then followed the main road straight ahead, asking any students or teachers I saw on the way. I went around in a circle and couldn't get an answer, so I turned back towards the school gate, and that's when I ran into you."

"You should look for the Student Affairs Office or the Dormitory Management Center, there's definitely someone on duty there," Chen Guiliang said. "I don't know where the Student Affairs Office is, but the Dormitory Management Center must be around here."

Jiang Junlai was rather puzzled. "How do you know?"

Chen Guiliang said, "It's not yet time for returning students to come back to campus, so right now it's mainly first-year freshmen and older students who didn't go home for the summer. And it's nighttime, so student activity basically has nothing to do with classrooms. Most students are coming from our left and then heading towards the school gate. Or they're coming in from the school gate and walking to our left. Understand?"

"I understand, the dorm area is on the left. I even went to take a look, but there are too many dorm buildings over there," Jiang Junlai said.

Chen Guiliang sighed. "Sigh, you're a Math Olympiad kid who got into Beida on a recommendation. Can't you use a little of your divergent thinking? There's a whole bunch of dorm buildings here, which means the Dormitory Management Center is nearby!"

Am I that stupid? Jiang Junlai scratched his head.

This classmate in front of him seemed quite smart.

"You also won a first prize in an academic competition, right?" Jiang Junlai asked.

Chen Guiliang smiled. "I did indeed win a first prize."

Jiang Junlai thought to himself: I didn't see this person at the Math Olympiad winter camp, he's probably from the physics or chemistry competition.

Chen Guiliang casually asked two passersby and soon arrived at the Yanyuan Dormitory Management Center.

Jiang Junlai's expression was particularly awkward at this moment. This place was only two or three hundred meters from the school gate, and he had just passed it three times...

Chen Guiliang walked in and struck up a conversation as if he knew everyone. "You've worked hard, teacher, still on duty so late."

The teacher was quite young, otherwise he wouldn't have been left on duty.

After looking at their admission notices, he flipped through the dorm assignment sheet and said, "Yuanpei Program students have been moved to Buildings 36 and 37 this year. Hmm... a few are in Building 38 too. One of you is in liberal arts and one is in sciences, you can share a room. Do you want to choose one yourselves?"

He pointed to the chart. "There are still five rooms to choose from."

Just as Jiang Junlai leaned in to look, he heard Chen Guiliang say, "I'll take 404 in Building 36."

"Then I'll take 404 too," Jiang Junlai said without much thought.

The teacher added, "There's no need to handle temporary check-in. You can just move in directly and complete the procedures tomorrow during registration. As for the mattress, quilt, pillow and all that, I'll have the building manager take you to get them. Oh, you also need to report the room number you chose to the building manager. You can get the key from the dorm supervisor in Building 36."

"Thank you, teacher." Chen Guiliang bowed very politely.

The teacher then called over a middle-aged woman, who was presumably the building manager for Building 36.

The woman's surname was Yang, so Chen Guiliang and Jiang Junlai called her Auntie Yang.

Auntie Yang led them two hundred meters south, then turned and walked four hundred meters west, pointing to an old dorm building. "That's Building 36."

Chen Guiliang memorized the route and location, thinking to himself: It's quite close to go outside the South Gate for BBQ or to an internet cafe from here.

Along the way, Auntie Yang also told them where the public bathrooms were, where they could use washing machines (for a fee), and so on.

She then took them to pick up their bedding and other supplies.

"I'm in charge of your Building 36, so if you have any difficulties in your daily life, just come find me. That includes things like a light bulb burning out."

"Thank you, Auntie Yang."

After the building manager left, Jiang Junlai said, "Auntie Yang is quite warm-hearted. By the way, what's your name?"

"Chen Guiliang."

"Sounds a bit familiar."

They arrived in front of Building 36, only to see some women's clothes hanging out to dry from the windows of the first and second floors.

"There can't be a mistake, right? This seems to be a girls' dorm," Jiang Junlai mumbled, unable to resist glancing at the clothes again.

Chen Guiliang, however, walked straight in and said to the dorm supervisor on duty, "Hello, Uncle, we're here to get our keys."

The dorm supervisor looked at their forms and reminded them as he got the keys, "The first and second floors are girls' dorms. Even if a girl invites you, you can't go in. If you get caught, the consequences are very serious."

"Understood," Chen Guiliang replied.

As they went upstairs, Jiang Junlai said excitedly, "I can't believe it's a co-ed dorm!"

Chen Guiliang corrected him, "This is called a co-ed building. Are you thinking of running down to the first and second floors for a tour?"

"You're the one who's thinking about it!" Jiang Junlai's face turned beet red.

Despite his words, Jiang Junlai was still very curious and made a point to observe as they went up the stairs. The entrance to the staircase on the girls' floors had an extra door installed; you couldn't get in without a key.

They arrived at 404 and pushed the door open.

Both of them simultaneously checked the living conditions.

Jiang Junlai was a bit disappointed. "No toilet, no bathroom, not even a faucet. It's about the same as our high school dorm."

"It's not bad, it's a four-person room."

Chen Guiliang opened his suitcase, took out a towel, and went outside to find the water room.

Sure enough, the layout here was just like a high school dorm. At the end of the hallway were a public toilet and a water room, and the water room had a washstand for doing laundry.

Chen Guiliang hadn't brought a bucket, basin, or toiletries; he would have to buy them tomorrow.

But he was covered in sweat from the heat during the day and was too lazy to go look for the public bathhouse outside. He simply turned on a faucet, soaked his towel, and gave himself a quick wash by splashing cold water on his body.

Slogging back to 404 in his wet sandals, Chen Guiliang found Jiang Junlai asleep.

This guy had taken a long train ride all the way from Guizhou; he was probably exhausted from the journey.

Chen Guiliang also laid out his palm-fiber mattress and cooling mat and lay down to rest.

He took out his phone and saw dozens of unread text messages. Seven were from Tao Xue, and four were from Bian Guanyue.

He quickly replied that he had checked into his dorm at Beida, then closed his eyes, planning to sleep for a while.

"Knock, knock, knock!"

A knock sounded at the door.

Jiang Junlai abruptly shot up from his bed and scrambled over to open the door.

Standing outside was a boy wearing a plaid shirt.

"Hello," said Jiang Junlai.

The boy in the plaid shirt introduced himself, "My name is Long Xiang, and I'm about to start my third year. You're new students in the Yuanpei Program, right?"

"Yes," said Jiang Junlai.

Long Xiang said, "There are only a dozen or so Yuanpei freshmen who haven't registered yet. I saw the light on in this room, so I came over to have a look. I might be your counselor."

"A third-year senior is a counselor?" Chen Guiliang also sat up.

Long Xiang explained, "Each counselor is responsible for ten freshmen, maybe one or two more. Third-year Yuanpei students apply for the position themselves. I thought it would be interesting to mentor you guys, so I volunteered."

"How are the advisors assigned?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Long Xiang said, "Advisors are divided into major advisors and part-time advisors. One major advisor also mentors ten students, occasionally one or two more. Part-time advisors are assigned only at crucial times, and they are all top professors at Beida. If you can build a good relationship with a part-time advisor, you could participate in an academic project as early as the second semester of your sophomore year."

"Holy crap!" Jiang Junlai exclaimed in amazement.

Long Xiang continued, "Your Yuanpei class is particularly brilliant. There are fewer than 150 students in total, but there are 10 provincial top scorers, 20 first-prize winners of academic competitions, and 3 international gold medalists in chemistry. Oh, and one first-prize winner of the New Concept Writing Competition. As for the rest, apart from those who got in through independent admission, they're basically all in the top ten of their province's arts or science tracks, or are city top scorers."

"By the way, what are your names? And how did you get in?"

Jiang Junlai said, "My name is Jiang Junlai, guaranteed admission from the CMO."

"I'm Chen Guiliang, the one with the New Concept first prize." Chen Guiliang felt that he stood out for being a slacker.

Ten provincial top scorers, twenty first-prize winners of academic competitions, and three international gold medalists in chemistry. Faced with these classmates, Chen Guiliang couldn't compete in academics; he could only be the "mudslide" of this year's Yuanpei class.

"So you're Chen Guiliang," Long Xiang laughed. "A heroine from our class of '02, Ao, really likes your poem 'Voyage on the Boundless Sea'. She even argued with people on the BBS over your poem."

It suddenly clicked for Jiang Junlai. "No wonder it sounded familiar. I knew it once you mentioned 'Voyage on the Boundless Sea'. There's a guy in my class who really admires you and would recite your poems in the classroom."

"I'm flattered by the kindness of both of your classmates. Please thank them for me," Chen Guiliang said with a smile.

Long Xiang added, "Let me get your contact info, QQ or phone number is fine. I'll notify you right away of any school arrangements."

Chen Guiliang gave his QQ and phone number, while Jiang Junlai only gave his QQ.

Chen Guiliang asked, "Senior Long, can I find the Veritable Records of the Ming Dynasty in the library?"

Long Xiang was taken aback for a moment, then took out his phone. "I'll ask for you."

He made several calls and finally hung up, saying, "The main library has the Veritable Records of the Ming Dynasty, as well as the index tools for it."

"Thank you, Senior Long," said Chen Guiliang.

Long Xiang smiled. "You're something else, asking about this stuff before military training even starts. I've taken history as an elective before, just to rack up credits, but I still haven't decided on my major."

"You haven't decided on a major in your third year?" Jiang Junlai was extremely surprised.

"It's normal," Long Xiang said. "Our advisors tell us to choose our major based on our interests and ambitions. I don't know what I'm interested in, and I don't have any ambitions for now. I can only audit classes I'm interested in and accumulate credits first, so I don't fail to graduate later."

Long Xiang reminded Chen Guiliang, "You're a liberal arts student, so don't hesitate when choosing your courses, especially the required ones. My roommate in my first year was a liberal arts student. Faced with all the courses in the university, he dithered, not knowing what to choose. But advanced math was mandatory. By the time he went to choose his course, the sections for Advanced Math D were already full, so he had to bite the bullet and choose Advanced Math C. It was extremely painful for him at first, and he even failed it once."

"What happened then?" Jiang Junlai asked curiously.

Long Xiang said, "After he failed Advanced Math C, he felt really ashamed, so he didn't bother with the make-up exam. He just re-took Advanced Math A and battled with math all day long. Last semester, he decided to go in the direction of computer science, with a minor in philosophy. He's currently using a computer to create some kind of philosophical model."

Chen Guiliang: "..."

The world of top students is difficult for ordinary people to comprehend.

(Cameos of top-ranking patrons will appear successively. The Senior Ao in this chapter is also a cameo, not the female lead. Also, thanks to a reader for the reminder, the Feiyu Internet Cafe outside Beida's South Gate was demolished in 2003.)

(Requesting monthly tickets at the end of the month.)
